item.title: Improving Razmyslov's (1974) bound: the Nagata-Higman index is at most $n^2-2$ for $n\ge3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.26641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $d(n)$ be the least $m$ such that every associative (not necessarily unital) algebra over a field of characteristic zero satisfying the identity $x^n=0$ also satisfies $x_1x_2\cdots x_m=0$; this is the Nagata-Higman index. Razmyslov proved $d(n)\le n^2$ in 1974; Kuzmin proved $d(n)\ge n(n+1)/2$ and conjectured equality; this is the Kuzmin (1975) conjecture. We prove $d(n)\le n^2-2$ for $n\ge3$ (and, by a simpler case of the same method, $d(n)\le n^2-1$ for $n\ge2$); in particular $d(6)\le34$. To our knowledge, $n=6$ is the first case in which the new bound improves the known bounds, and this is the first improvement of Razmyslov's bound for general $n$. For $m=n^2-1$ and $m=n^2-2$, Formanek's criterion reduces $d(n)\le m$ to the statement that no nonzero linear combination of $(m+1)$-cycles lies in one particular isotypic block of the group algebra of $S_{m+1}$. For $m=n^2-1$ this statement follows from the branching rule; for $m=n^2-2$ we prove it using the Jucys-Murphy elements and a theorem of Frobenius on the characters of the alternating group. These bounds have also been proved in the Lean proof assistant.
item.dc:creator: Dave Goel

item.title: The Construction of Directed Partial Orders on the Complex Field by Puiseux Series and Stratification
item.description: arXiv:2611.26644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Birkhoff and Pierce asked in 1956 whether the complex field C admits a lattice order compatible with the ring operations. Schwartz and Yang proved in 2011 that C admits directed partial orders. We give a new construction that by using a transcendence basis of C over Q, we embed C into a field of Puiseux series F{{s}}, so that every complex number acquires a series expansion, and we define positivity by a condition on the leading coefficient. Every directed partial order we construct is placed in a stratification by how much of the expansion a rule has to read. Reading one term, a window of fixed width, or a sensitivity condition on small changes, we obtain five nested conditions and six types. Relative to the fixed level valuation, cones satisfying B correspond to the cards satisfying a product and a sum condition. Cones satisfying C are never lattice orders, which excludes Types 1, 2, 3. We give an example of Type 4 that is not a lattice order either. The existence of a lattice order on C and the existence of orders of Types 5 and 6 still remain open. This is a stratification rather than a complete classification because only Types 1 - 4 are shown to be nonempty.
item.dc:creator: Zitian Zhu

item.title: Nonlinear skew Lie-type centralizers on $\ast$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.26647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(\mathcal{A}\) be a unital \(\ast\)-algebra over the complex field \(\mathbb{C}\), with center \(\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})\). For any \(X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_n\in\mathcal{A}\), define recursively $ p_1(X_1)=X_1,$ $p_2(X_1, X_2)=[X_1,X_2]_{\ast}=X_1X_2-X_2X_1^{\ast}$ and $p_n(X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_n)=[p_{n-1}(X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_{n-1}),X_n]_{\ast}$ for all integers \(n\geq 2\). In this paper, we prove that if a map \(\Phi:\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{A}\) satisfies $\Phi(p_n(X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_n))=p_n(\Phi(X_1),X_2,\ldots,X_n)$ for all \(X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_n\in\mathcal{A}\), then \(\Phi\) necessarily has the form $\Phi(X)=ZX,$ where \(Z=Z^{\ast}\in\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})\). As an application, we establish that, under suitable assumptions, every nonlinear generalized skew Lie \(n\)-derivation \(G:\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{A}\) admits a standard form $G(X)=ZX+D(X),$ where \(Z\in\mathcal{Z}(\mathcal{A})\) and \(D:\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{A}\) is an additive \(\ast\)-derivation. Finally, we apply this result to several important classes of unital \(\ast\)-algebras, including unital prime \(\ast\)-algebras, standard operator algebras, and von Neumann algebras.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Afajal Ansari, Mohammad Ashraf, Md Shamim Akhter

item.title: On coherence of enveloping algebras of infinite-dimensional Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.27824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate when the universal enveloping algebra $U(\mathfrak{g})$ of an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ is coherent. We show that if $\mathfrak{g}$ is the loop algebra of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{h}$ then $U(\mathfrak{g})$ is coherent exactly when $\mathfrak{h}$ is nilpotent. As a consequence, we show that $U(\mathfrak{g})$ is not coherent if $\mathfrak{g}$ is complex, simple, $\mathbb{Z}$-graded, of polynomially bounded growth, and not isomorphic to the Witt algebra $W = \mathrm{Der} \mathbb{C}[t,t^{-1}]$ or its one-sided version. We also demonstrate that the homomorphic image of $U(W)$ used to prove non-Noetherianity of $U(W)$ in previous work of the first author and Walton is not coherent. On the other hand, we establish that two closely related connected graded rings are graded coherent. Finally, we prove that any exhaustively filtered ring is coherent if its Rees ring is graded coherent.
item.dc:creator: Susan J. Sierra, James Timmins

item.title: Quotients of Leavitt path algebras over commutative rings by graded ideals
item.description: arXiv:2402.04155v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $E$ be a graph and $R$ a unital commutative ring. We study quotients of the Leavitt path algebra $L_R(E)$ by graded ideals which, unlike in the case of field coefficients, need not be basic. Using the saturated functions of Rigby and van den Hove, we introduce $I$-basic graded ideals, where $I$ is an ideal of $R$, and we prove that, for an arbitrary graph $E$, the quotient of $L_R(E)$ by an $I$-basic graded ideal is isomorphic to the Leavitt path algebra of a quotient graph of $E$ with coefficients in $R/I$. More precisely, for every graded ideal there is a canonical epimorphism from such an algebra onto the quotient, and it is an isomorphism if and only if the graded ideal is $I$-basic. This extends a result of Larki for basic graded ideals. We also introduce graded ideal functions, defined on the vertices of $E$ and on the pairs $(H,v)$ formed by a hereditary saturated set $H$ and a breaking vertex $v$ of $H$, and we show that they form a lattice isomorphic to the lattice of graded ideals of $L_R(E)$. As an application, for a finite graph $E$ in which no cycle has an exit, we describe the quotient of $L_R(E)$ by any graded ideal as a direct sum, indexed by the sinks and the cycles of $E$, of Leavitt path algebras over quotient rings of $R$, namely matrix algebras over quotient rings of $R$ and of $R[x,x^{-1}]$. Finally, examples on the infinite binary tree and Toeplitz graph show that the hypothesis on the finiteness and cycles cannot be removed.
item.dc:creator: Sevgi Harman, M\"uge Kanuni, Guillermo Vera de Salas

item.title: Structure of the Cayley-Dickson algebras
item.description: arXiv:2505.11747v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Viewing the Cayley-Dickson process as a graded construction provides a rigorous definition of associativity consisting of three classes, which divides the non-associ\-ative parts into four types. These simplify the Moufang loop identities and Malcev's identity and categorise non-associative loops. Analysing the non-associativity structure of sedenions and higher level Cayley-Dickson algebras uncovers octonion and three quasi-octonion, power-associative subalgebras. Power-associativity is proved to grow by multiples of seven that introduce zero divisors in factors of 84 for all Cayley-Dickson algebras. It is convenient to replace the terminology hypercomplex numbers with ultracomplex numbers to capture the fact that sedenions and all higher level Cayley-Dickson algebras contain quasi-octonions that are ultracomplex. The non-associative types reduce the 84 zero divisors in sedenions via three cycles and four modes down to seven primary zero divisor pairs of two-term sums of basis elements providing new techniques to analyse the seven quasi-octonions loops in sedenions. The graded notation allows the eight octonion and seven quasi-octonion subalgebras of sedenions to be uniquely derived, up to representation. The zero divisors for split sedenion algebras are analysed and mappings between three of these are described showing 180 zero divisors and the other split algebra is analogous to sedenions with 84 zero divisors. These split algebras are shown to involve quasi-octonion algebras with mixed signature.
item.dc:creator: G. P. Wilmot

item.title: Tangent Lie Algebras of Automorphism Groups of Free Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2507.20486v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study an analogue of the Andreadakis-Johnson filtration for automorphism groups of free algebras and introduce the notion of tangent Lie algebras for certain automorphism groups, defined as subalgebras of the Lie algebra of derivations. We show that, for many classical varieties of algebras, the tangent Lie algebra is contained in the Lie algebra of derivations with constant divergence. We also introduce the concepts of approximately tame and absolutely wild automorphisms of free algebras in arbitrary varieties and employ tangent Lie algebras to investigate their properties. It is shown that nearly all known examples of wild automorphisms of free algebras are absolutely wild -- with the notable exceptions of the Nagata and Anick automorphisms. We show that the Bergman automorphism of free matrix algebras of order two is absolutely wild. Furthermore, we prove that free algebras in any variety of polynilpotent Lie algebras -- except for the abelian and metabelian varieties -- also possess absolutely wild automorphisms.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Shestakov, Ualbai Umirbaev

item.title: Succinct Strict Pair Certificates for Reduced Groebner Bases
item.description: arXiv:2601.06765v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify verification of supplied strict critical-pair witnesses for Groebner bases in a graph model with shared polynomial and exponent computations. Over the rationals, unrestricted verification in two variables is polynomial-time many-one equivalent to identity testing for powerful skew circuits over the integers. The reverse reduction uses a fixed two-element reduced Groebner basis and preserves the formal monomial bound on every witness it constructs. The forward reduction gives a one-sided-error randomized polynomial-time verifier without a support bound. We also prove matching bounds on certificate length for explicit families. For a bivariate family indexed by $k$, literal shifts require $\Theta(k^2)$ bits, shared exponent computations require $\Theta(k)$ bits, and an expanded certificate requires $\Omega(k2^k)$ bits. For a multivariate family with $K=\sum_i k_i$, the bounds are $\Theta(nK+\sum_i k_i^2)$ for full shift vectors and $\Theta(K\log_2(n+1)+\sum_i k_i^2)$ for sparse shift labels.
item.dc:creator: Chandrasekhar Gokavarapu, Lakshmi Gayathri Isukapalli, Janardhana Rao Kolli, Fathima Sulthana Md, Sai Durga Rolla

item.title: Twisted generalized Weyl Poisson algebras of type $(A_1)^n$
item.description: arXiv:2606.08263v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a generalization of generalized Weyl Poisson algebras. This is a Poisson analogue of the twisted generalized Weyl algebras defined by Mazorchuk and Turowska. We prove existence of these algebras in two ways, using Ore extensions and by using skew Laurent Poisson algebras. It is shown that this structure is preserved under tensor products, Poisson twists, and by taking invariant rings. Finally, we prove a simplicity criterion for these Poisson algebras.
item.dc:creator: Jason Gaddis

item.title: A note on the image of graded multilinear polynomials on upper triangular matrices
item.description: arXiv:2606.17243v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the image of polynomials multilinear in graded variables evaluated on the algebra of upper triangular matrices endowed with a group grading. We show that, in general, such an image need not be a vector subspace. However, under the additional assumption that the identity component of the grading is commutative, we prove that the image is always a vector subspace. We further investigate the image of polynomials evaluated on inverse and direct limits of algebras. As a consequence, we prove that the image of a polynomial evaluated on a direct limit of upper triangular matrix algebras whose identity component is commutative is always a vector subspace.
item.dc:creator: Adison Tim\'otio Silva, Felipe Yukihide Yasumura

item.title: Positive definite matrices and involutions: the manners of their infinite cousins
item.description: arXiv:2607.25134v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Matrices and involutions in/on the algebras $B(\mathbb{R})$ and $B(\mathbb{C})$ of real (resp., complex) row- and column-finite $\omega\times\omega$ matrices are studied. It is proved that any positive definite $\mathbb{R}$-algebra involution on $B(\mathbb{R})$ (resp., any positive definite conjugate-linear involution on $B(\mathbb{C})$) is given by conjugating the transpose involution (resp., the conjugate-transpose involution) with a positive definite matrix from the algebra in question. All positive definite matrices in these algebras have Cholesky factorizations within the algebra. Examples are constructed to show that such positive definite matrices need not have any eigenvalues for their canonical action on column-finite column vectors, and they need not have any square roots in $B(\mathbb{C})$.
item.dc:creator: Pere Ara, Ken Goodearl, Kevin C. O'Meara

item.title: A negative exponent range for Audenaert's complementary McCarthy trace inequality
item.description: arXiv:2608.20937v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Audenaert introduced a class of complementary McCarthy type trace inequalities in his work on completely monotone functions and Bernstein functions; the same problem was later included in the problem list of Audenaert and Kittaneh. The known results cover the corresponding directions for $q\le -2$, $0<q\le 1$, $1\le q\le 2$, and $2\le q\le 3$, while the negative range $-2<q<0$ was left as a conjectural case. We prove the negative exponent inequality, in fact for every $q<0$. After the inversion $X=A^{-1}$, $Y=B^{-1}$, the problem reduces to a trace inequality for the parallel sum $X:Y$. The proof uses the Kubo--Ando mean chain, an Ando--Hiai type log-majorization for matrix geometric means, and a finite-dimensional Schatten H\"older inequality, including the quasi-norm range. We also record that the positive exponent side $q\ge 3$ follows directly from Audenaert's norm-compression inequality for positive semidefinite $2\times2$ block matrices, and in fact holds for all $q\ge 2$. Finally, we determine the equality case on the negative side: equality holds if and only if $A=B$.
item.dc:creator: Xing Li, Bin Zhou

item.title: Automorphisms of Free Metabelian Lie Algebras, II
item.description: arXiv:2610.21954v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that every automorphism of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ of rank $n\geq 4$ over an arbitrary field $K$ is almost tame; that is, it can be expressed as a product of Chein automorphisms (also called one-row transformations). Moreover, we prove that, for $n\geq 4$, the group $\mathrm{Aut}(M_n)$ of all automorphisms of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ over a field $K$ of characteristic not equal to $3$ is generated by its linear automorphisms, together with a single quadratic and a single cubic automorphism. The same result holds for fields of any characteristic if $n\geq 5$.
item.dc:creator: Ualbai Umirbaev

item.title: A Non-linearizable Action of $S_3$ on Free Metabelian Lie and Associative Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.26060v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $M$ be the free metabelian Lie algebra of rank $4$ over the field of complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$. We construct a non-linearizable action of the symmetric group $S_3$, the smallest nonabelian group, on $M$ by automorphisms. We also construct a non-linearizable action of $S_3$ on free metabelian associative algebras of rank $4$.
item.dc:creator: Altyngul Naurazbekova, Ualbai Umirbaev

item.title: Associativity conditions for linear quasigroups and equivalence relations on binary trees
item.description: arXiv:2310.09184v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We characterise the bracketing identities satisfied by linear quasigroups with the help of certain equivalence relations on binary trees that are based on the left and right depths of the leaves modulo some integers. The numbers of equivalence classes of $n$-leaf binary trees are variants of the Catalan numbers, and they form the associative spectrum (a kind of measure of non-associativity) of a quasigroup. Every group-based equivalence relation arising here can be replaced by one defined by an abelian group generated by at most two elements. The fine associative spectra form a lattice isomorphic to the lattice of rank-two subgroups of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with an additional least element. This classifies the equivalence relations completely; closed formulas for all their numbers of classes remain open.
item.dc:creator: Erkko Lehtonen, Tam\'as Waldhauser

item.title: An introduction to the symmetric group algebra
item.description: arXiv:2507.20706v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This is an introduction to the group algebras of the symmetric groups, written for a quarter-long graduate course. After recalling the definition of group algebras (and monoid algebras) in general, as well as basic properties of permutations, we introduce several families of elements in the symmetric group algebras $\mathbf{k}[S_n]$ such as the Young--Jucys--Murphy elements, the (sign-)integrals and the conjugacy class sums. Then comes a chapter on group actions and representations in general, followed by the core of this text: a study of the representations of symmetric groups (i.e., of left $\mathbf{k}[S_n]$-modules), including the classical theory of Young tableaux and Young symmetrizers. We prove in detail the main facts including the characterization of irreducible representations (in characteristic $0$), the Garnir relations, the standard basis theorem, the description of duals of Specht modules, and the hook length formula, as well as a number of less known results. Finally, we describe several bases of $\mathbf{k}[S_n]$ that arise from the study of Specht modules, including the Murphy cellular bases. The methods used are elementary and computational. We aim to assume as little as possible of the base ring $\mathbf{k}$, and to use as little as possible from representation theory (nothing more advanced than Maschke and Jordan--H\"older). Over 100 exercises (without solutions) are scattered through the text.
item.dc:creator: Darij Grinberg

item.title: Lie Algebra Decomposition Classes for Reductive Algebraic Groups in Arbitrary Characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2511.01440v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the decomposition classes of the Lie algebras of connected reductive algebraic groups, over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. We extend some results proved previously under restrictions on the characteristic, including a formula for the dimension of a decomposition class, and introduce Levi-type decomposition classes to account for some of the difficulties encountered in bad characteristic. We also establish properties of Lusztig--Spaltenstein induction of non-nilpotent orbits, such as parabolic independence, extending the known results for nilpotent orbits. Finally, we determine the covering relation for the closure order on decomposition classes, in the case of good characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Joel Summerfield

item.title: The generalized Dixmier conjecture and the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.33919v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture $\mathrm{JC}_2$ implies the generalized Dixmier conjecture $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ for the first Weyl algebra $A_1$, which states, in one of several equivalent formulations, that every endomorphism of the two-by-two matrix ring $\operatorname{Mat}_2(A_1)$ is invertible. To study the converse, we associate to each endomorphism of $\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb C}$ with Jacobian one a family of holonomic $A_2(k)$-modules over finite fields $k$. Kontsevich's conjecture predicts the existence of a $\mathcal D$-module in characteristic zero, unique up to isomorphism, whose reductions to positive characteristic are isomorphic to the prescribed modules. We prove uniqueness whenever such a lift exists. If these lifts exist for every such endomorphism, then $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ implies $\mathrm{JC}_2$. For every $n\ge2$, we construct a Lagrangian subvariety of $T^*\mathbb A^n$ that provides a counterexample to Kontsevich's conjecture. We also study an ultraproduct version of the lifting problem: whether these finite-field modules can be recovered as reductions of a single module in characteristic zero along a chosen ultrafilter. We prove that this is possible precisely when the Berest--Wilson invariants of these modules, regarded as left $A_1(k)$-modules, are bounded along that ultrafilter. Finally, we study two other conjectures of Kontsevich on arithmetic support, giving a counterexample to one and partial results on the other.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Kanel-Belov, Timofey Fedorov

item.title: Solutions of the set-theoretic quantum Yang-Baxter equation arising from posets
item.description: arXiv:2611.15540v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Victoria Lebed observed that the map $(x, \, y) \mapsto (\min\{x, \, y\}, \, \max\{x, \, y\})$ on a totally ordered set is an idempotent solution of the braid equation. We extend this example in several directions, by constructing four families of solutions of the braid equation associated to posets. First, for a given poset $P$, the map $R_P$ which sorts the comparable pairs and fixes the incomparable ones is an idempotent solution of the braid equation whose automorphism group is the automorphism group of the poset $P$. Combined with the classical theorem of Birkhoff, this shows that every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of an idempotent solution of the braid equation of the form $(P, \, R_P)$, for some poset $P$. Moreover, $R_P \cong R_Q$ if and only if $P \cong Q$, and the solutions of the form $R_P$ are exactly the idempotent solutions of the braid equation which permute the components of each pair. Secondly, we classify all the solutions $R$ of the braid equation on an arbitrary set $X$ such that $R(x, \, y) \in \{(x, \, y), \, (y, \, x)\}$ for all $x$, $y\in X$: they are exactly the solutions $R_{\mathcal{P}}$ associated to the decompositions $\mathcal{P}$ of $X$ into posets. Finally, we associate to any finite poset $P$ two involutive solutions $D_P$ and $E_P$ of the braid equation, whose automorphism groups are $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^P \rtimes {\rm Aut} (P)$ and, if $P$ is connected and has at least two elements, the group of automorphisms and anti-automorphisms of $P$.
item.dc:creator: Gigel Militaru

item.title: The Bapat-Sunder eigenvalue conjecture fails over the reals
item.description: arXiv:2611.23269v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In 1986 Bapat and Sunder asked whether $\operatorname{per}(A)$ is the largest eigenvalue of $F_A=[a_{i,j}\operatorname{per}(A(i,j))]$ for every positive semidefinite Hermitian $A$, where $A(i,j)$ deletes row $i$ and column $j$. Drury disproved this over the complex field in 2018 and conjectured that the property holds for real positive semidefinite matrices. We disprove Drury's conjecture with a rank-$4$, $32\times32$ integer Gram matrix and an integer vector whose Rayleigh quotient exceeds $\operatorname{per}(A)$; verification uses integer arithmetic. Together, the two counterexamples resolve the Bapat-Sunder eigenvalue conjecture negatively over both fields. Counterexamples exist of every order $n\ge32$. As an application to quantum optics, the violation yields a $36$-mode orthogonal interferometer and a direction of relative arrival-time delays among $32$ photons with identical-variance Gaussian wave packets along which every sufficiently small nonzero delay increases the probability that all photons are detected within four designated output modes.
item.dc:creator: Logan R. Chalmers
